heard: The most famous labor strike in history didn't even happen on Earth. In November 1973, NASA launched three rookie astronauts to America's first space station, Skylab. Gerald Carr, Edward Gibson, and William Pogg soon struggled under an incredibly micromanaged 84-day schedule. When the astronauts tried to hide an early case of space sickness, NASA's chief astronaut Alan Shepard issued a stern reprimand. Exhausted and overworked, the crew suffered an accidental radio error that caused them to miss a scheduled daily briefing. This 90-minute radio gap was immediately sensationalized by the media as a deliberate and unprecedented mutiny in orbit. After the schedule was lightened, the crew became more productive than ever, yet none of them ever flew in space again. which means that history is most famous.
